features.feature_value: Use vulgarity/ethics (e.g., vulgar or victim-blaming) as the cutoff, even while considering free speech
features.evidence_span: I looked for the level of vulgarity... If it was vulgar or victim blaming, I took it down. It's basic ethics.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes a decision rule based on vulgarity and ethical concerns.

features.feature_value: Prophane/violent content leads to removal for both versions
features.evidence_span: if i seen profanity or violence in the messages, that when i decided to not allow either.
features.rationale: They set a direct criterion that profanity or violence triggers disallowing.

features.feature_value: Removal when inflammatory; only civil discussion should be allowed
features.evidence_span: If they were inflammatory I tossed them. The only way to have a discussion is to be civil.
features.rationale: Their criterion centers on inflammatory content and maintaining civility.

features.feature_value: Allow opinions unless posts verge on inciting violence against specific people, which should be deleted
features.evidence_span: if they're inciting violence against specific people than that a problem and I would've said to delete those posts.
features.rationale: They reference a specific content cue (incitement/violence targeting) that changes the decision.

features.feature_value: Seeing the posts side-by-side helps them avoid bias and focus on whether each enables healthy debate
features.evidence_span: Seeing both posts side-by-side puts the words into perspective... I was just trying to focus on the core of each post and whether or not it would provide a well-intentioned space for healthy debate or discussion.
features.rationale: They directly connect the pair-comparison format to a strategy for fairer evaluation.

features.feature_value: Even if they respect the right to express views, they reject abusive language
features.evidence_span: they have the right to express them... I do not believe that teh abusive language used in a few of the posts should be allowed to be shared.
features.rationale: They state a split criterion: rights to express vs. disallowing abusive language.

features.feature_value: Decision driven by preventing harm or unjustified negative influence, while favoring free speech
features.evidence_span: if it would cause harm or negative influence for no reason... I am a believer in free speech so I like to allow most things through.
features.rationale: They name harm/negative influence as the deciding factor while otherwise allowing broadly.

features.feature_value: Hard to make one joint decision because they opposed one of the posts
features.evidence_span: It was hard to make a single joint decision on both posts because I technically opposed one of them.
features.rationale: They describe a process difficulty specific to pairing decisions.
